Overview

This company handbook document is a consolidated reference for working at Redwood. It covers our culture and expectations, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding overview, and a concise internal tools guide. The intent is to give new and existing employees a single, practical resource to answer common questions and find the right owners for follow-up.

## 1) Working at Redwood - culture & expectations

Short intro:
Redwood is an engineering-first company that prioritizes reliability, developer experience, and measurable outcomes. We expect every employee to act with ownership, collaborate across teams, and communicate clearly.

Core principles:
- Customer-first product thinking: build with production economics and developer workflows in mind.
- Measured reliability: ship with SLOs and monitor regressions.
- Empathy & clarity: document decisions and share context.
- Continuous improvement: iterate on production metrics and developer feedback.

Day-to-day expectations:
- Be present at team standups or asynchronously update your status.
- Use PR reviews to ship evaluative changes; aim for clear descriptions and test coverage.
- Keep runbooks and docs updated as part of any operational change.

## 2) Roles & career ladders

Purpose:
Provide clarity about common role families at Redwood and the expectations for career progression. This section summarizes typical IC and manager ladders and the skills we evaluate during calibration.

Role families (examples):
- Engineering: Software Engineer I/II/Senior/Staff/Principal, SRE, Infra Engineer, Runtime Engineer
- Product: Product Manager, Senior PM, Group PM
- Applied ML & Research: Applied ML Engineer, Research Engineer, Model Ops
- Developer Experience: SDK Engineer, Docs Engineer, Solutions Engineer
- GTM functions: Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Partnerships

Career ladder highlights (what we evaluate):
- Ownership & impact: scope owned and measurable outcomes (SLO improvements, cost reductions, customer enablement).
- Technical depth: ability to design system architecture, mentor others, and lead large technical efforts.
- Collaboration & communication: cross-functional leadership, clarity in docs and PRs.
- Execution & delivery: consistent on-time delivery, quality, and incident response.

Promotion process (high level):
1. Prepare a promotion packet: updated resume/role-specific doc, 3-5 signal projects, metrics of impact, peer and manager endorsements.
2. Submit to people-ops and manager for initial review.
3. Calibration / panel review: 4-6 reviewers from across engineering & product review packet and provide feedback.
4. Decision & feedback: people-ops communicates outcome and next steps.

Promotion checklist (table):
| Evidence | Example artifacts |
|---|---|
| Impact metrics | Token-cost reduction, latency improvement (p50/p95), revenue/usage metrics |
| Technical leadership | Design docs, ADRs, code ownership areas |
| Mentorship | Mentees promoted, org knowledge transfer sessions |
| Cross-team influence | Successful rollouts with other teams, runbooks adopted org-wide |

## 3) Benefits & perks

Summary:
Redwood offers a competitive benefits package designed to support health, financial security, and work-life balance. Below is a concise inventory and the primary owners for questions. For full plan details and vendors, see People Ops benefits portal (link).

Key offerings (table):
| Category | What we provide | Owner / contact |
|---|---|---|
| Health & Dental | Medical (multiple plan tiers), dental, vision | people-ops@redwood.ai |
| Family & Parental | Parental leave (primary: 20 weeks), fertility support, adoption reimbursement | people-ops@redwood.ai |
| Financial | 401(k) with match, RSU grants, annual salary review | finance@redwood.ai |
| Wellbeing | Mental health sessions, employee assistance program (EAP) | people-ops@redwood.ai |
| Time off | Flexible PTO, 12 company-wide holidays, discretionary shutdowns | people-ops@redwood.ai |
| Learning & Growth | Learning stipend ($1,500/year), conference budget, mentorship program | L&D (people-ops)

Perks & allowances (bulleted):
- Home office stipend for remote-first hires ($800 one-time onboarding).
- Monthly co-working/commute allowance for qualifying roles.
- Quarterly team offsites budget (manager approves).
- Discounts with partner providers and cloud credits for developer experimentation.

How to raise benefits questions:
1. Check the People Ops benefits portal for plan docs and FAQs.
2. Submit a ticket to the People Ops Slack channel (#people-ops) or email people-ops@redwood.ai.

## 4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy:
We hire for technical ability, product judgment, and collaboration. Interviews are structured to reduce bias: role-specific rubrics and at least one cross-functional interviewer.

High-level hiring process (numbered):
1. Requisition & role definition: Hiring manager writes a clear role spec and required competencies.
2. Sourcing & screening: Talent identifies candidates and completes a 30-minute screen.
3. Technical loop & cross-functional interviews: role-appropriate coding/design exercise, work-sample review, and behavioral interviews scored against rubric.
4. Offer & negotiation: People Ops generates offer letter, coordinates compensation and start date.
5. Background check & onboarding docs: run by people-ops; contingent offers must clear background checks where required.

New hire onboarding checklist (table):
| Day/Week | Task | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-start | Complete HR forms, set up SSO & 2FA, equipment request | people-ops, IT |
| Day 0 | Welcome packet, team intro, manager 1:1 scheduled | manager, people-ops |
| Week 1 | Access to repos, runbooks, onboarding projects, doc tour | manager, buddy |
| Month 1 | First project milestone, goals for 90-day plan | manager |
| Month 3 | Calibration check-in, OKR alignment, feedback session | manager, people-ops |

New hire first 7 days (quick steps):
1. Complete IT & HR tasks (SSO, payroll, benefits enrollment).
2. Join core Slack channels: #all, #eng, #product, team channel.
3. Meet your onboarding buddy and schedule recurring 1:1s.
4. Read key docs: runtime-architecture, infra-standards, api-standards (links in Related resources).
5. Clone primary repos and run the local quickstart.

Manager responsibilities during onboarding (short list):
- Clear 90-day goals and initial project scope.
- Assign a buddy and protect time for ramping.
- Ensure necessary access and environment working by day 3.

## 5) Internal tools & access guide

Purpose:
A brief catalog of the most-used internal tools and the primary owners, plus how to request access and where to find runbooks.

Primary tools (bulleted list):
- Identity & SSO: Okta - Admins: IT Security. Onboarding: submit IT ticket.
- Code hosting: GitHub (org: redwood-inference) - Repo access governed by team membership. Request via GitHub Teams app or people-ops.
- CI/CD: Buildkite - Owners: eng-infra. Checkout pipelines in project README.
- Cloud consoles: AWS & GCP projects - Access through IAM groups; request via #infra-access.
- Observability: Datadog & Honeycomb - Dashboards in /dashboards; escalation runbooks in eng-platform/runbooks.
- Docs & Knowledge: Confluence (this space) - Content owners listed at top of pages. Use templates for ADRs and runbooks.
- Support & Tickets: Zendesk for external customer tickets; internal issues tracked in linear or JIRA depending on team.

Access request procedure (numbered):
1. Determine required groups from the access matrix (link to infra-accounts-and-networking).
2. Open an access request in the IT ticketing system, include justification and manager approval.
3. IT grants access and documents time-limited elevated access where needed.
4. Validate access and notify your manager and buddy.

Security & least-privilege reminders:
- Request the minimal set of permissions for your role and region.
- For elevated debug sessions, request time-boxed access and document actions taken.
- Keep machine secrets out of code; use KMS/HSM-backed secrets manager.

## 6) Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Q: Who do I contact about payroll or expenses?
A: finance@redwood.ai for payroll; expenses via the Expensify/Concur integration.

Q: How do I request parental leave?
A: Contact people-ops@redwood.ai and provide expected dates; People Ops will walk you through paperwork and benefits.

Q: Where do I find production runbooks?
A: Confluence > eng-sre > runbooks. If you can\u2019t find an entry, ping the on-call SRE or eng-sre@redwood.ai.
